mainEntity.name: How much does a Volkswagen Golf 1.5 TSI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Volkswagen Golf 1.5 TSI engine replacement typically costs £2,500-£5,000 supply-only for a rebuilt unit, depending on engine code and whether it's a standard TSI or eTSI mild-hybrid. Used engines start from £800-£2,200. Fitting adds approximately £780-£1,300 in labour (12-20 hours at independent specialist rates). Main dealer fitted prices are typically 30-50% higher.

mainEntity.name: Does the Volkswagen Golf 1.5 TSI have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The EA211 1.5 TSI engine uses a timing belt, not a chain. VW's official guidance has changed over time - early EA211 engines had a 5-year / 80,000-mile replacement interval, but more recent advice suggests periodic inspection only. However, many specialists recommend replacing the belt at 80,000-100,000 miles or around 5-6 years as a precaution.

mainEntity.name: Is the VW Golf 1.5 TSI engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.5 TSI (EA211 evo) is generally considered one of the more reliable petrol engines in the Golf range. However, owners report issues including excessive oil consumption, water pump failure, and turbocharger actuator problems. Regular maintenance with the correct VW-spec oil (0W-20) is essential.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the 1.5 TSI and 1.5 eTSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.5 TSI is a standard turbocharged petrol engine with no electrification. The 1.5 eTSI is a mild-hybrid that adds a 48V belt-integrated starter generator and a small 48V lithium-ion battery. The eTSI provides coasting capability (engine off while driving), improved start-stop performance, and slightly better fuel economy.

mainEntity.name: Why does my Golf 1.5 TSI use so much oil?

acceptedAnswer.text: Excessive oil consumption is one of the most significant concerns with the 1.5 TSI engine. Some owners report needing to top up oil between services, with consumption of 0.5-1.0 litres per 1,000 miles. VW has issued technical bulletins addressing the issue. If your Golf is using more than 1 litre of oil between services, have it inspected - piston ring replacement or engine replacement may be required.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Volkswagen Golf 1.5 TSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a Mk7.5 Golf 1.5 TSI (2017-2020) worth £8,000-£16,000, a rebuilt engine at £2,500-£5,000 plus fitting may represent 25-50% of the vehicle's value. Replacement is usually viable if the car is otherwise in good condition. For Mk8 Golf models (£12,000-£30,000), replacement is almost always worthwhile. For higher-mileage Mk7.5 models with multiple issues, a used engine may be more cost-effective than a rebuilt unit.

historyTimeline.h2: Volkswagen Golf 1.5 TSI / eTSI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Volkswagen Golf 1.5 TSI arrived in 2017 as part of the seventh-generation (Mk7.5) Golf facelift, replacing the 1.4 TSI with VW's new EA211 evo engine family. The 1.5 TSI introduced variable turbine geometry (VTG) turbocharging - a technology previously reserved for Porsche - along with Active Cylinder Technology (ACT) and Miller cycle combustion. In 2020, the eighth-generation Golf (Mk8) launched with both standard 1.5 TSI and mild-hybrid 1.5 eTSI variants, the latter pairing the petrol engine with a 48V belt-integrated starter generator for improved efficiency and coasting capability.

milestones.description: Mk7.5 Golf facelift introduced 1.5 TSI 130hp (CD15GX) and 150hp (DADA) petrol engines
1.5 TSI 150hp with 7-speed DSG (DA15EM, DA15EX) added to the range
Mk8 Golf launched with 1.5 TSI 130hp (DPBA/DPB) and 1.5 eTSI 150hp mild-hybrid (DA15EX)
EA211 evo2 engine update with revised emissions hardware and improved efficiency
1.5 TSI and eTSI engine line-up updated for Euro 6e emissions compliance

commonProblems.h2: Volkswagen Golf 1.5 TSI / eTSI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Volkswagen Golf 1.5 TSI (EA211 evo) is VW's advanced turbocharged petrol engine, featuring variable turbine geometry (VTG) turbocharging, Active Cylinder Technology (ACT), and Miller cycle combustion. The 1.5 eTSI adds a 48V mild-hybrid system for improved efficiency and coasting. While generally reliable, the engine has documented issues including excessive oil consumption, water pump failure, timing belt concerns, and turbocharger actuator problems. Rebuilt Golf 1.5 TSI and eTSI engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Excessive Oil Consumption - Why the Volkswagen Golf 1.5 TSI Burns Oil
problems.rootCause: One of the most significant concerns with the 1.5 TSI engine is excessive oil consumption. Some owners report needing to top up oil between services. The issue appears to affect certain production batches more than others. VW has issued technical bulletins addressing oil consumption on some EA211 evo engines.

repairOptions.longevity: If oil warning light is frequent

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip engine, replace rings, inspect bores

repairOptions.longevity: When oil consumption is severe or engine has suffered damage

problems.recommendation: For Golf 1.5 TSI owners, preventative maintenance is key. Monitor oil levels regularly - if you're topping up more than 1 litre between services, have the engine inspected. Replace the water pump at the first sign of coolant loss. For eTSI owners, ensure the 48V system is checked at every service. If oil consumption is severe or water pump failure has caused overheating, a replacement engine with upgraded components and warranty often represents better long-term value than chasing individual repairs.

problems.h4: Water Pump & Cooling System Failure - EA211 evo Weakness
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Golf 1.5 TSI / eTSI (all EA211 evo variants, 2017-present)
problems.rootCause: The water pump and thermostat housing on the 1.5 TSI are known to fail prematurely. Leaks develop around the housing, causing coolant loss and potential overheating. VW Group water pump failures are well-documented across EA211 engines.

repairOptions.longevity: If coolant leak is detected early
When overheating has caused head gasket or bottom-end damage

problems.h4: 48V Mild-Hybrid System Issues - eTSI Specific Problems
problems.rootCause: The 1.5 eTSI's 48V mild-hybrid system adds complexity. Battery failures, DC-DC converter issues, and software glitches can trigger warning lights and reduced performance. The 48V battery is also expensive to replace.
